answer: Each agent may open only a small number of new credit lines, and a line counts only after its counterparty has repaid several independent loans on time. This makes identity alone worthless: a swarm of fresh accounts cannot vouch itself into trusted status. To expand, the attacker must fund real transactions, wait through repayment rounds, and risk losing collateral on defaults. A meadow market might track yarrow shipments along each trust thread, but the costly part is earning reliable history, not minting names.
